tool.name: host_header_check
tool.description:
Probe a URL for host-header injection / cache-key trust issues. Detects whether the target trusts attacker-controlled values in `Host:` / `X-Forwarded-Host:` / `X-Forwarded-Server:` / `X-Host:` / `Forwarded:` / `X-Forwarded-For:` and reflects them into responses — the primitive behind password-reset link poisoning, cache poisoning, and cookie-scope leaks.
Probes (each is one HTTP request, all bounded by `timeout`):
| Probe | Mutation | |---|---| | `host_replace` | `Host: ` | | `host_suffix` | `Host: .` (suffix-anchored allowlist bypass) | | `xfh` | `X-Forwarded-Host: ` | | `xfs` | `X-Forwarded-Server: ` | | `x_host` | `X-Host: ` | | `forwarded` | `Forwarded: host=` (RFC 7239) | | `xforig` | `X-Forwarded-For: ` | | `dual_xfh` | `Host:` + `X-Forwarded-Host:` together |
Detection looks for the attacker host in: - `Location` / `Content-Location` / `Refresh` / `Link` headers → **high** (CWE-20, host_header_injection) — direct redirect-to-attacker primitive - `Set-Cookie` `Domain=` attribute → **high** (CWE-20) — cookie scope leak - response body → **medium** (CWE-20) — info_disclosure / link-building gadget - cached response with body-length variance under header mutation, no explicit reflection → **low** (CWE-444, cache_poisoning) — cache-key obliviousness candidate
Each finding includes `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (the §11 non-tech UX fields) so the wrapper renders dashboard cards with concrete fix instructions (allow-list trusted host headers at the reverse-proxy edge; never derive cookie `Domain=` from `Host:` / `X-Forwarded-Host:`; configure a fixed base URL for password-reset / signup / OAuth callback URL builders).
Read-only (GET only, no follow-redirects so reflected `Location` is observable). Probe payloads include a unique random subdomain per run so findings are auditable in the target's logs and don't collide with any pre-existing `attacker.example.com` references.
Composes with cluster-A safety: `--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` / `--auth-*` apply to every probe automatically.

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: URL to probe. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Path component preserved (probes hit the same path as the baseline). Examples: `example.com`, `https://app.example.com/login`, `https://api.example.com:8443/`.

parameter.name: attacker_host
parameter.description: Override the base attacker host used in probes (default `attacker.example.com`). A unique random subdomain is auto-prepended to make every run's probes uniquely identifiable in the target's logs.

returns.description:
{success, target_url, target_host, attacker_host, baseline: {status, body_length, has_location, looks_cached}, probes: [{label, mutation_note, status, reflection: {body, location_header, cookie_domain_header, other_header}, cache_poison_signal, finding_severity, finding_kind, evidence}, ...], findings_emitted}.
The agent should follow up high-severity `location_reflection` findings by manually triggering a flow that builds a link from the host header (password-reset, signup, OAuth callback) and confirming the link points at the attacker.
